name: Burlington Northern
description: Burlington Northern was formed on March 2, 1970, from Great Northern, Northern Pacific, Chicago, Burlington & Quincy, and Spokane, Portland & Seattle. During its 25-year independent existence, BN expanded and rationalized its network and absorbed the St. Louis–San Francisco Railway (Frisco) in 1980. Burlington Northern Inc. and Santa Fe Pacific combined on September 22, 1995; their operating railroads remained separate until ATSF merged into Burlington Northern Railroad on December 31, 1996.

paintSchemes.name: Cascade Green
paintSchemes.description: Cascade Green became Burlington Northern’s standard corporate paint scheme after its formation in 1970. A green body, dark roof, white BN logos and road numbers, and diagonal white nose striping defined its original identity and preceded later distinct BN variants.

paintSchemes.name: White Face
paintSchemes.description: White Face emerged in the late 1980s as a variation of Cascade Green. It retained BN’s green body and dark roof while expanding the white cab-face treatment, becoming the railroad’s standard late-era variation of the Cascade Green identity.

photo.caption: BN 2755 in White Face
photo.credit: George H. Menge / Don Ross Collection / Don’s Rail Photos

paintSchemes.name: Executive / Grinstein Green
paintSchemes.description: Executive / Grinstein Green was a late BN scheme and a departure from the earlier green-bodied styles. A cream body, dark green upper section, thin red stripe, black lower band, and bold black BN markings defined the look most closely associated with BN’s SD70MAC fleet.

photo.caption: BN SD70MAC #9479 and #9737 in Executive / Grinstein Green
